note_on_method: Layers run vertically, raw material to patient. ZONES run horizontally: each is a chain of its own through those layers, and a node carries the zone it belongs to in its "zone" field. Two layers are bridges -- primary packaging and bioprocess tools -- shared by every zone, and their nodes carry the zone "BR". Each company appears exactly once. A node whose price_symbol_kind is "none" is drawn and never scored; three nodes are priced but deliberately kept out of every basket, and say so in their notes. Every price line was measured against the price vendor on 2026-09-25.
benchmark_note: XPH is the equal-weight US pharmaceutical line. Equal weight because EW_MAP, the benchmark that actually scores a question here, is equal-weight too, so the second line is built the same way; and pharmaceutical rather than healthcare because this map is not about insurers or hospitals. The gap, stated rather than hidden: XPH is US-only and holds no CDMO, no bioprocess tools and no distribution, so it does not span roughly forty percent of this map. The same kind of gap GRID has for the power map and ITA for the defence one.

value.en: The physical supply chain behind medicine — seven chains, from Chinese key starting materials to the pharmacy shelf, and where each one breaks.

desc.en: A living map of the medicine supply chain in seven zones — generics and Chinese API, sterile injectables, biologics, radiopharma, cell and gene, incretins and distribution — with {nodes} companies, {cps} chokepoints pulsing with the market, a forecast board and questions with a date.

story.en: A linchpin is the small pin that holds the wheel on the axle. Pull it and everything stops. We find those pins in the supply chain, and measure what happens to them — every day.

footer.en: Linchpin Signal · not investment advice · every number carries a source

layers.name: Raw materials and KSM
layers.description: Key starting materials and the basic chemistry every downstream step assumes it can buy.

layers.name: API and peptides
layers.description: Active ingredient, made to order or to stock. The layer the tariff schedule names alongside the finished drug.

layers.name: Manufacturing and CDMO
layers.description: Contract development and manufacturing: biologics, sterile drug product, and the capacity nobody owns enough of.

layers.name: Primary packaging
layers.description: Everything the drug touches. Shared by every zone on this map, which is why it is drawn as a bridge.

layers.name: Bioprocess tools
layers.description: Consumables, filtration and instruments. The other bridge: a line has to be equipped before it can fill anything.

layers.name: Brands
layers.description: The companies whose names are on the box, across all seven chains.

layers.name: Distribution
layers.description: Three wholesalers move most of the medicine in the United States.

edges.what: Biologics capacity, and the exposure policy names

chokepoints.name: China-only key starting materials

blurb.en: Moving finished-dose production does not help when every supplier buys the same upstream chemical from the same country. Nearly 41 percent of the key starting materials in US-approved APIs come solely from China.

chokepoints.concentration: Nearly 41 percent of KSMs used in US-approved APIs come solely from China; China controls 94 percent of amoxicillin raw materials, 74 percent of the US crude heparin supply and 55 percent of global acetaminophen API. Nearly seven hundred medicines approved in the United States depend on at least one chemical made only in China
chokepoints.substitute: Indian and Western KSM capacity, which is being built into the same demand rather than standing spare

chokepoints.name: Sterile injectable capacity

blurb.en: The most shortage-prone category in the pharmacy: low-margin, hard to make, and made on lines that are old, few and shared.

chokepoints.concentration: A small number of qualified sterile lines, several of them decades old, carrying products whose price does not fund replacing them
chokepoints.substitute: Another maker's line, after a regulatory transfer that is measured in quarters

chokepoints.name: Medical isotope supply

blurb.en: A radioligand is made, shipped and injected against a clock. Lutetium-177 has a useful life measured in days, so a missed reactor window is a missed dose.

chokepoints.concentration: A handful of reactors and generators worldwide, with actinium-225 available only in clinical quantities and molybdenum-99 behind most nuclear imaging
chokepoints.substitute: New reactor and cyclotron capacity, all of it years out

chokepoints.name: Biologics CDMO capacity

blurb.en: Large-scale biologics capacity is booked years out, and policy has narrowed who may take the work.

chokepoints.concentration: A short list of houses able to absorb work at scale, with the largest China-based incumbent under a policy cloud
chokepoints.geography: Switzerland, South Korea, China, Japan, United States
chokepoints.substitute: Samsung Biologics, Lonza and Fujifilm, all adding into the same demand

chokepoints.name: Primary packaging and containment

blurb.en: Every zone on this map ends at the same handful of component makers. A stopper is qualified to its molecule, so a second source is a regulatory change and not a purchase order.

chokepoints.concentration: High-value components were 49 percent of West's sales in the second quarter of 2026, with GLP-1 elastomer alone about a tenth of company revenue
chokepoints.substitute: A qualified second supplier, where one has already been through the filing

chokepoints.name: Section 232 tariff exposure

blurb.en: A 100 percent duty on patented drugs and on the API and key starting materials behind them, with generics and nuclear medicines exempt for now and Commerce due to report on whether that holds.

chokepoints.concentration: The proclamation issued 2 April 2026 took effect on 31 July 2026 for the seventeen companies named in Annex III and on 29 September 2026 for everyone else, with reduced rates for the EU, Japan, Korea and Switzerland
chokepoints.geography: United States, European Union, Japan, Korea, Switzerland
chokepoints.substitute: Onshoring commitments and most-favoured-nation pricing deals, which is what the schedule is designed to buy
chokepoints.substitution_time: not applicable -- this is policy, not capacity
